doc.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Bostic, Washington clubs and arriving in New York
title: After hours at the Caverns with Blanche Calloway
summary: He remembers the Caverns, Blanche Calloway running it, and meeting Ruth Brown there.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: What was happening on the after-hours side?

Let’s see. On the after-hours side, where was it? After hours in Washington. I don’t remember too much after hours in Washington. If there was, I probably wasn’t old enough to get in it. After hours in Washington. I can’t – I don’t have no comprehension of.
Oh, it may have been the Caverns. It might have been the Caverns.
Were you aware of Benny Caldwell, who that was?
No. When I was going to the Cavern, it was Cab Calloway’s sister.

Blanche Calloway. She was running it. She had – the m.c., his name was George Craft, he was a gay guy that was the m.c. He was a singer and the m.c. I remember that crew. I don’t know who was before that or after that. That’s where I remember meeting Ruth Brown, because she was – turned out to be Ruth Brown’s manager.
Blanche. So that’s where I met Ruth Brown. She brought her there to sing, and I played for her.
At that point, was it the Caverns, or the Crystal Caverns, or what was it?
The Caverns. What was the inside? Was it white?

No, it was the same kind of a cavern-looking thing. They did some things to it over the years, but basically it’s still like with the stuff hanging from the ceiling. It looked like a cave. It looked like a cave in there for a minute. Because I remember what’s-his­ name jumping up and down with his horn and hitting his head on them spikes that was coming down from the ceiling: Leo Parker. Wild antics and stuff. So it was basically like a cave.
